PERF-029.name: Fresh Object, Array or Function Passed to Memoised Children or Dependencies on Every Render
PERF-029.question: Does this component create a new object, array or function on each render and hand it to a memoised child, a context provider or a hook dependency list, defeating the memoisation?

javascript: an inline object, array or arrow function passed as a prop to a component wrapped in React.memo or PureComponent, inside a large list or a frequently re-rendered parent
<Context.Provider value={{ ... }}> with an object literal built during render, re-rendering every consumer
an object, array or function built in the component body and listed in a useEffect, useMemo or useCallback dependency array, so the hook runs on every render
an expensive computation over a large collection run directly in the render body on every render
the value is wrapped in useMemo or useCallback with correct dependencies, or defined outside the component
the child is not memoised and the tree is small, so the extra render is negligible
the React Compiler or a signal-based framework handles memoisation

distinguish_from.REL-322: the dependency list is missing a value, a correctness fault rather than wasted renders
distinguish_from.PERF-006: the repeated computation does not involve a render or memoised component

PERF-030.name: Growing Collection Copied on Every Iteration
PERF-030.question: Does this function rebuild a growing array, list, map or object by copying all of it on each step of a loop or reduction, making the whole run quadratic?

javascript: reduce((acc, x) => ({ ...acc, [k]: v }), {}) or reduce((acc, x) => [...acc, x], []) over an input-sized array
arr = arr.concat(x), arr = [...arr, x] or obj = { ...obj, [k]: v } inside a loop
python: items = items + [x], t = t + (x,) or d = {**d, k: v} inside a loop
np.append, np.concatenate, np.vstack, pd.concat or DataFrame.append called per iteration on the accumulated result
rust: a Vec, String or map cloned and extended on each iteration, or acc = [acc, item].concat() in a fold
cpp: a container or string copied and reassigned each iteration, such as v = v + x for a user type or s = s + piece on a long string

any: the accumulator is changed in place with push, append, insert or +=, or pieces are collected and joined once at the end
the loop has a small fixed bound

distinguish_from.PERF-004: the value rebuilt each time is a text string joined piece by piece
distinguish_from.PERF-013: the container grows in place and only lacks a capacity reservation

PERF-031.name: Row-by-Row Loop Over Array or DataFrame Data
PERF-031.question: Does this function loop in Python over the rows or elements of a NumPy array or pandas DataFrame to do work that a single vectorised operation would do?

python: for i, row in df.iterrows(), df.itertuples() or range(len(df)) with df.loc[i] or df.iloc[i] used to compute or assign per row
df.apply(func, axis=1) for arithmetic, comparisons or string operations that column expressions provide
a Python for loop over the indices of a large NumPy array doing element-wise arithmetic, comparison or accumulation
column or array expressions, np.where, groupby, merge or a built-in reduction do the work
each row needs a call with no vectorised form, such as a network request, or the data is known to be small

distinguish_from.PERF-025: the loop order works against the array's storage order, in any language
distinguish_from.PERF-030: the cost comes from copying a growing result each iteration

PERF-032.name: Client, Pool or Connection Built on Every Call
PERF-032.question: Does this function construct a costly reusable client on each call, such as an HTTP client, connection pool or database connection, instead of using a shared one?

any: a request handler or frequently called helper that opens a new database connection, creates a connection pool or builds an SDK client each time it runs
an HTTP client or session with its own TLS setup and connection pool created per request and dropped afterwards
python: requests.get or requests.post called repeatedly against one host with no Session, or boto3.client(...), create_engine(...) or httpx.Client() inside the function
javascript: new PrismaClient(), new Pool(...), mongoose.connect or new S3Client(...) inside a handler
rust: reqwest::Client::new() or a database pool built inside a handler or loop
c: curl_easy_init and cleanup, or a full connect and TLS handshake, for each request to the same server

any: the client is created once at module, application or struct level and passed in or reused
the function runs once per process, such as a script entry point or start-up code

distinguish_from.CWE-1050: the resource is acquired inside a loop in this function, once per iteration
distinguish_from.PERF-008: the repeated cost is the request itself, whose result could be cached

PERF-033.name: Linear Scan or Length Recount Repeated Inside a Loop
PERF-033.question: Does a loop in this function repeat an operation that walks a string or sequence from the start each time, such as recounting its length or seeking to a position?

c: strlen(s) in a loop condition or body over the same string, or strcat onto one growing buffer in a loop
cpp: std::advance, std::next or std::distance on std::list or forward iterators inside a loop over positions
python: lst.index(x), lst.count(x) or s.count(x) inside a loop over the same data, or len(list(generator)) recomputed each pass
rust: s.chars().nth(i), s.chars().count() or iter.nth(i) inside a loop over i, or a linked list indexed by position

any: the length or position is computed once before the loop, or an iterator, pointer or index is carried forward
the sequence offers constant-time length and indexing, or is short and fixed

distinguish_from.PERF-007: the repeated scan is a membership or key search that a set or map would replace
distinguish_from.PERF-004: the cost is building a string by repeated concatenation in a language with immutable strings

PERF-034.name: Avoidable Allocation Inside a Hot Loop
PERF-034.question: Does a loop in this function allocate and free heap memory on every iteration where one buffer could be reused or the allocation moved outside?

c: malloc or calloc and free of a scratch buffer of the same size inside a loop body
cpp: a std::vector, std::string, std::map or std::function constructed inside a loop body and filled each time, or make_shared or new per element where values would do
rust: Vec::new(), String::new(), format!, to_string(), to_vec(), collect() into a temporary or Box::new inside a loop that runs per item of a large input

any: the buffer is created once outside the loop and cleared or overwritten each pass
the allocated value is kept, moved into a collection or returned, so it is needed per item
the loop runs a small fixed number of times

distinguish_from.PERF-013: one container grows across iterations without a reserved capacity
distinguish_from.PERF-014: a large existing value is copied rather than a new one allocated

PERF-035.name: More Columns or Fields Fetched Than the Function Uses
PERF-035.question: Does this function fetch whole records, wide rows or large payloads and then use only a few of their fields?

any: SELECT * or an ORM call loading full entities, including large text or binary columns, where the code reads one or two fields
a related collection or nested document loaded in full only to read an id, a name or a count
an API called for a full resource representation when a field mask, projection or lighter endpoint exists and only a small part is used
python: Model.objects.all() or session.query(Model) iterated for one attribute, with no only(), values(), values_list() or load_only()
javascript: findMany or find with no select or projection, then map(x => x.id)

any: the query names the columns it needs or uses a projection, or most fetched fields are used
the row is small, or the full entity is passed on to code that needs it

distinguish_from.PERF-002: too many rows are loaded, rather than too many fields per row
distinguish_from.PERF-019: rows are fetched only to count them or test that one exists
